boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.1 opens with the dateline וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗ית בַּשִּׁשִּׁי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ אֲנִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנָ֑י וַתִּפֹּ֤ל עָלַי֙ שָׁ֔ם יַ֖ד אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (sixth year, sixth month, fifth day) carrying the hand-of-YHWH idiom in its אדני יהוה form (tier-1 vision onset; the construct-only sweep counts 7 hand-of-YHWH verses book-wide, of which this is the only one carrying the double divine name), immediately followed by the transport at oshb:Ezek.8.3 וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ תַּבְנִ֣ית יָ֔ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֖נִי בְּצִיצִ֣ת רֹאשִׁ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ בֵּֽין הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם וַתָּבֵא֩ אֹתִ֨י יְרוּשָׁלְַ֜מָה בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה צָפ֔וֹנָה אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֣ם מוֹשַׁ֔ב סֵ֖מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַמַּקְנֶֽה (the Spirit lifts the prophet and sets him at Jerusalem's inner-court gate — tier-1 vision transport, sweep: 20 verses book-wide) and the phrase במראות אלהים “in visions of God” (sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 1:1, 8:3, 40:2, the three vision-transport frames). Close: oshb:Ezek.8.6 ends the directed “lift up your eyes” scene with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲרֹאֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה מהם עֹשִׂ֑ים תּוֹעֵב֨וֹת גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עֹשִׂ֣ים פֹּ֗ה לְרָֽחֳקָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וְעוֹד֙ תָּשׁ֣וּב תִּרְאֶ֔ה תּוֹעֵב֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת, the prophet's first sight of the image of jealousy and the promise “you will again see yet other great abominations,” which turns the page to the next scene rather than closing the vision; a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.8.6 (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to a seam here even though no oracle-refrain formula is present. Both sides: the onset side is triple-marked (dateline, hand, transport) and is the strongest onset in the book; the close side rests on the samekh plus the forward-pointing “again see” formula rather than a recognition or utterance refrain, so the row is held below high confidence.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.7 וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י אֶל פֶּ֣תַח הֶֽחָצֵ֑ר וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֹר אֶחָ֖ד בַּקִּֽיר — a fresh transport (“he brought me to the door of the court”, sweep: 20 verses) opens a new tableau, paired with the “son of man, dig now in the wall” command at oshb:Ezek.8.8. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.13 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה תּוֹעֵב֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִֽׂים repeats the “you will again see” transition that also closed the row before it, signalling the end of the elders'-idolatry tableau (Jaazaniah and the seventy elders censing before wall-carvings “in the dark,” saying “Yahweh doesn’t see us”) and the turn to the next abomination. Both sides: a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.8.6 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to the seam behind it, even though the onset verse itself is a clean transport with no competing formula; the close has no Masoretic mark at all (no pe or samekh follows 8:13) and rests solely on the repeated “again see” device, which is disclosed as weaker, tier-4-adjacent evidence rather than a refrain-grade close.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.14 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת הַתַּמּֽוּז, a third transport (“he brought me to the door of the gate of Yahweh's house”) opening the Tammuz-weeping tableau; a samekh follows this very verse (single-witness), which is disclosed as evidence that could instead argue a shorter row ending at 8:15 (see rejected alternative). The row is extended through a second transport at oshb:Ezek.8.16 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (the sun-worshippers, “about twenty-five men… their backs toward Yahweh's temple”) because no refrain or mark separates 8:16-18 from what precedes it. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.18 וְגַם אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם is the wrath declaration — “I will also deal in wrath… I will not hear them” — a narrative and thematic close (the fourfold tableau's climax) rather than a recognition or utterance refrain; oshb:Ezek.9.1 opens the next scene with the loud-voiced cry that sets the executioners in motion, which is the strongest available onset-side confirmation that 8:18 is where the temple-tour proper ends.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.9.1 וַיִּקְרָ֣א בְאָזְנַ֗י ק֤וֹל גָּדוֹל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר קָרְב֖וּ פְּקֻדּ֣וֹת הָעִ֑יר וְאִ֛ישׁ כְּלִ֥י מַשְׁחֵת֖וֹ בְּיָדֽוֹ — the loud cry summoning the city's executioners — is the scene's own hard onset (no transport verb here; the prophet remains where 8:18 left him and instead hears a cry, which the strategy's own scene-seam catalogue treats as the 8/9 boundary). Close: oshb:Ezek.9.11 וְהִנֵּ֞ה הָאִ֣ישׁ לְבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַקֶּ֨סֶת֙ בְּמָתְנָ֔יו מֵשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר עָשִׂ֕יתִי כאשר צִוִּיתָֽנִי, the man clothed in linen reporting “I have done as you have commanded me,” is a narrative task-completion close; a samekh follows this same verse (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration exactly at the row's end. Both sides: the onset (the cry) has no formula but is a scene-change as strong as a transport verb in this vision's own idiom; the close pairs a narrative completion with a samekh, a strong Masoretic corroboration for this row's own close.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.1 וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֶל הָרָקִ֨יעַ֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל רֹ֣אשׁ הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים כְּאֶ֣בֶן סַפִּ֔יר כְּמַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כִּסֵּ֑א נִרְאָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם opens the throne-like sapphire vision with no transport verb and no formula at all — the scene continues directly from 9:11 with a bare “then I looked, and behold”. The row is anchored instead on the glory's own movement: oshb:Ezek.10.4 וַיָּ֤רָם כְּבוֹד יְהוָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַכְּר֔וּב עַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּמָּלֵ֤א הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֶת הֶ֣עָנָ֔ן וְהֶֽחָצֵר֙ מָֽלְאָ֔ה אֶת נֹ֖גַהּ כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה records כבוד יהוה rising from the cherub to the threshold of the house (sweep: 9 verses book-wide carry כבוד יהוה — 1:28, 3:12, 3:23, 10:4, 10:18, 11:23, 43:4, 43:5, 44:4, the departure/return arc), the first stage of the glory's exit. Close: oshb:Ezek.10.8 וַיֵּרָ֖א לַכְּרֻבִ֑ים תַּבְנִית֙ יַד אָדָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵיהֶֽם — the hand of a man under the cherubim's wings — closes the coal-taking errand before the row turns to the extended wheel description. Both sides: a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.9.11 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to the seam behind it, even though the onset verse oshb:Ezek.10.1 itself carries no mark; the close carries no parashah mark either (chapter 10 carries none at all, disclosed below), so the close-side seam rests on content alone — the coal-fire task is complete and the following verses shift from narrated action to sustained physical description.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.9 וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה אוֹפַנִּים֮ אֵ֣צֶל הַכְּרוּבִים֒ אוֹפַ֣ן אֶחָ֗ד אֵ֚צֶל הַכְּר֣וּב אֶחָ֔ד וְאוֹפַ֣ן אֶחָ֔ד אֵ֖צֶל הַכְּר֣וּב אֶחָ֑ד וּמַרְאֵה֙ הָא֣וֹפַנִּ֔ים כְּעֵ֖ין אֶ֥בֶן תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ turns from the coal-taking action to a sustained physical description of the four wheels (“the appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone”), echoing the wheel-vision of chapter 1 (the “river Chebar” inclusio device, sweep: 8 verses book-wide, three of them at oshb:Ezek.10.15, oshb:Ezek.10.20 and oshb:Ezek.10.22). Close: oshb:Ezek.10.17 בְּעָמְדָ֣ם יַעֲמֹ֔דוּ וּבְרוֹמָ֖ם יֵר֣וֹמּוּ אוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ הַחַיָּ֖ה בָּהֶֽם — “for the spirit of the living creature was in them” — ends the description with a summary clause before oshb:Ezek.10.18 resumes narrated action (the glory's departure). Both sides: as with the row before it, no parashah mark and no K/Q sit anywhere in this span (chapter 10 carries none), so the seam is argued from the shift between static description and resumed narration alone; this is disclosed as the weakest-anchored row in the part.

It is kept as its own row because it is a bytes-verifiable, self-contained descriptive block (the wheel vocabulary אוֹפַ֣ן (oshb:Ezek.10.9) and הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל (oshb:Ezek.10.13) does not recur outside 10:6-17 and 1:15-21) bounded by narrated action on both sides.

device_notes: Held at low confidence per the standing instruction that this is a result, not a failure: the “row or texture” question for this span could not be settled from the staged formula inventory, and the bespoke rationale above is the reason. boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.18 וַיֵּצֵא֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד עַל הַכְּרוּבִֽים resumes narrated action — כבוד יהוה goes out from the threshold and stands over the cherubim, the second stage of the glory's departure begun at 10:4. Close: oshb:Ezek.10.22 וּדְמ֣וּת פְּנֵיהֶ֔ם הֵ֣מָּה הַפָּנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ עַל נְהַר כְּבָ֔ר מַרְאֵיהֶ֖ם וְאוֹתָ֑ם אִ֛ישׁ אֶל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵֽכוּ completes the “river Chebar” identification (“the faces which I saw by the river Chebar… they each went straight forward”), immediately before oshb:Ezek.11.1 opens a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate”) that continues from the very place — the east gate — where 10:19 had just stood the cherubim. Both sides: the onset is corroborated by the glory-movement device (tier-1, sweep: 9 verses); the close has no parashah mark (chapter 10 carries none) but is corroborated by the double Chebar citation at 10:20 and 10:22 and by the clean handoff to 11:1's transport verb, which is the strongest close-side evidence available in this mark-free chapter.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.17 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל בְּנ֣וֹת עַמְּךָ֔ הַמִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וֹת מִֽלִּבְּהֶ֑ן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽן — “set your face against the daughters of your people” — is one of the book's 9 set-your-face verses and marks an addressee-class shift from the male prophets of 13:1-16 to women who prophesy “out of their own heart.” Close: oshb:Ezek.13.23 לָכֵ֗ן שָׁ֚וְא לֹ֣א תֶחֱזֶ֔ינָה וְקֶ֖סֶם לֹא תִקְסַ֣מְנָה ע֑וֹד וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י אֶת עַמִּי֙ מִיֶּדְכֶ֔ן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ן כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends “then you will know that I am Yahweh” in the second-feminine-plural form (וידעתן), distinct from both the 3mp-28 and the 2mp-21 counted recognition families and disclosed here as an uncounted gender variant; a matching 2fp clause also closes the magic-bands sub-paragraph at oshb:Ezek.13.21. Both sides: a pe follows oshb:Ezek.13.16 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness); the onset itself is tier-1 (set-your-face, address-class shift); the close is refrain-shaped but in a form outside either counted sweep, and no parashah mark falls exactly at 13:23, so the row is held at medium rather than high confidence.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.1 וַיָּב֤וֹא אֵלַי֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִזִּקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי — “then some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me” — is a bare narrative scene-opener with no formula; a pe follows this very verse (single-witness), and the word-event formula proper opens the next verse, oshb:Ezek.14.2 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר. The row opens at 14:1 rather than 14:2 because the elders' scene-setting is what the oracle answers (“should I be inquired of at all by them?”, 14:3). Close: oshb:Ezek.14.11 לְ֠מַעַן לֹֽא יִתְע֨וּ ע֤וֹד בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְלֹֽא יִטַּמְּא֥וּ ע֖וֹד בְּכָל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֣י לְעָ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה; a second pe follows this verse (single-witness), giving the row a pe on both its opening and its closing verse. boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.12 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, a strict word-event formula, opens the Noah-Daniel-Job oracle on personal versus vicarious righteousness. The unit is a sustained four-scourge refrain list (sword, famine, evil beasts, pestilence, each introduced “or if…”) and is never cut inside it, per the book's own guard against splitting a numbered or refrain-marked list; the triad refrain itself recurs, closing each scourge, with the utterance formula co-occurring at oshb:Ezek.14.14, 14.16, 14.18 and 14.20. Close: oshb:Ezek.14.23 וְנִחֲמ֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כִּֽי תִרְא֥וּ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֖ם וְאֶת עֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּי֩ לֹ֨א חִנָּ֤ם עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי בָ֔הּ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה ends the part with the utterance formula a fifth time, immediately before oshb:Ezek.15.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר opens the vine mashal with its own fresh strict word-event. A pe follows oshb:Ezek.14.23 (single-witness). Both sides are formula-clean and this closes the part.
